# GitHub Actions Security

Workflows and scripts under `.github/` run with the bot's credentials on behalf of whoever triggered them. The items below are blocking.

- [ ] **No PR code in privileged contexts** - `pull_request_target`, `workflow_run`, `issue_comment` and `repository_dispatch` (all `@pytorchbot` commands) workflows run with base-repo privileges, so they must not build, execute, or run tools from a checkout of PR code (git-only operations like rebase and push are fine), nor execute or restore artifacts and caches produced by PR runs (parsing them as untrusted data is fine). Approving an outside contributor's held CI runs (e.g. via `/actions/runs/{id}/approve`) counts as executing their code unless authorized as below
- [ ] **Authorize both the user and the commit** - Anyone can post a comment, including `@pytorchbot` commands, so before a privileged action check the commenter's write permission via the API, not `github.actor` or the comment itself. Tie the action to the immutable SHA that user vetted, never the current head, a branch ref, or author-controlled commit dates, and check that derived commits (e.g. rebases) add nothing beyond it and the trusted base branch
- [ ] **No injection of attacker-controlled strings** - Do not interpolate `${{ github.event.* }}` fields (PR title/body, comments, branch names, commit messages) or `github.head_ref` directly into `run:` or `actions/github-script` `script:`; pass them through `env:` and quote `"$VAR"`. Do not write such values to `GITHUB_ENV`, `GITHUB_PATH` or `GITHUB_OUTPUT` without validation
- [ ] **Least-privilege tokens and pinned actions** - In privileged workflows, declare `permissions:` explicitly (read-only by default, widened per job) and set `persist-credentials: false` on checkout unless a later step pushes. Pin new actions from outside `actions/*` and `pytorch/*` to a full upstream commit SHA, since their owners can move tags and branches
